result_1.name: JANUS Exact-Match / Independent-Future Incompatibility Lemma
result_1.statement: For discrete classical B,T, if B and T are statistically independent and Pr[B=T]=1, then both variables are the same deterministic point mass and therefore H(T)=H(B)=0.
proof_summary: Exact equality gives sum_x p_x q_x=1.
But sum_x p_x q_x <= max_x q_x <= 1.
Equality forces max_x q_x=1, hence T is deterministic; diagonal equality forces B to the same value.
result_1.conditional_corollary: If PRE_RETURN B_R is measurable from freeze-time view V_R, then Pr[B_R=T] <= p_guess(T|V_R)=2^{-H_min(T|V_R)}. Thus exact equality almost surely implies H_min(T|V_R)=0.
result_1.interpretation: A non-degenerate exact PRE_RETURN/future identity cannot coexist with a valid positive freeze-time conditional min-entropy premise under the admitted forward-null model. At least one premise must fail.
result_1.novelty_boundary: The underlying min-entropy/guessing-probability relation and elementary independence lemma are established information theory and are not claimed as new mathematics. JANUS contribution under review is their explicit use as an operational separator between bootstrap self-consistency and independent-future evidence.
